agree.reason: A GM who already likes the writer gets an honest, well-argued case, and conceding the renovation earns trust; but the memo never explains why an insider who has run this desk for seven weeks is a safer choice than an outsider from a bigger hotel, so the competing option stays open.

honest.reason: It rightly declines the writer's wish to claim being the main reason scores rose, but it has two small overstatements: 5 shifts out of 9 is a little over half the time, not 'almost half', and the heading 'I've kept the team together' takes credit for the lower turnover without evidence that the writer caused it.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the turnover figures into 64% vs 36% and four fewer departures, but it leaves out easy, favourable derived figures, such as about 20 trainee shifts saved last year (5 hires × 4 shifts) or the payroll value of that.

right_comparison.reason: It compares against how things were before (turnover, training length), but it never describes the real alternative the GM is weighing, an outside hire who would need time to learn this property and team, so the comparison that matters most is missing.

qualification.reason: The budget gap is admitted openly, but the only hedge is 'I'd value your view'; there is no checkable commitment such as a budget-training milestone with a date or payroll target that the GM could hold the writer to.

objections.reason: The GM's belief that the renovation drove the scores is met directly and fairly, and the budget gap is addressed, but the outside candidate's larger-hotel experience is never answered.

fit.reason: It's a brief, well-organised memo that fits on one page, which is exactly the written application asked for.
